"""Synchronous compatibility wrapper for the async fetcher."""

import asyncio

from .client import Client


def fetch_all(urls, transport=None):
    async def fetch():
        async with Client(transport=transport) as client:
            return await client.get_many(urls)

    return asyncio.run(fetch())

import asyncio

from fetcher import Client, FetchError, TransientError, aggregate
from fetcher.sync import fetch_all


def test_get_and_many():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as client:
            assert await client.get("http://x/1") == b"payload for http://x/1"
            results = await client.get_many(["http://x/1", "http://x/404"])
            assert results[0].startswith(b"payload")
            assert isinstance(results[1], FetchError)
        assert client.closed

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_retry_then_succeed():
    attempts = {"n": 0}

    async def flaky(url):
        attempts["n"] += 1
        if attempts["n"] < 3:
            raise TransientError("try again")
        return b"ok"

    async def run():
        client = Client(transport=flaky, retries=3, backoff=0)
        assert await client.get("u") == b"ok"
        assert client.calls == 3

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_get_many_limits_concurrency_and_preserves_order():
    active = 0
    peak = 0

    async def transport(url):
        nonlocal active, peak
        active += 1
        peak = max(peak, active)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
        active -= 1
        return url.encode()

    async def run():
        client = Client(transport=transport, max_concurrency=2)
        results = await client.get_many(["a", "b", "c", "d"])
        assert results == [b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d"]
        assert peak == 2

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_summarize():
    async def run():
        client = Client()
        assert await aggregate.summarize(client, ["http://x/1", "http://x/404"]) == {
            "ok": 1,
            "failed": ["http://x/404"],
            "bytes": len(b"payload for http://x/1"),
        }

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_sync_wrapper():
    assert fetch_all(["http://x/1"]) == [b"payload for http://x/1"]

from decimal import Decimal

from billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule


def test_simple_total():
    inv = build_invoice("A1", [("x", "10.00", 2), ("y", "0.50", 1)])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("20.50")
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("20.50")


def test_with_tax():
    inv = build_invoice("A2", [("x", "100.00", 1)], TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")))
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("119.00")


def test_discount_whole_numbers():
    inv = build_invoice("A3", [("x", "100.00", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10"))])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("90.00")


def test_discount_total_matches_sum_of_rounded_pdf_lines():
    inv = build_invoice(
        "A4",
        [
            ("x", "0.05", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10")),
            ("y", "0.05", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10")),
        ],
    )
    assert line_totals(inv) == [Decimal("0.05"), Decimal("0.05")]
    assert invoice_total(inv) == sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("0.10")

"""Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total()."""
from decimal import Decimal

from .discounts import apply_discount
from .invoice import Invoice
from .money import round_money
from .tax import tax_for


def line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line."""
    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]


def invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:
    """Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum."""
    net = sum(line_totals(inv), Decimal("0.00"))
    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))

import re
import unicodedata

_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def email_key(email):
    return email.strip().lower()


def name_key(name):
    """Key for matching names: casefolded, whitespace-normalized, no accents."""
    s = _WS.sub(" ", name.strip()).casefold()
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", s)
    return "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def dedupe(records):
    """records: list of dicts with 'name' and 'email'. Returns survivors in first-seen order."""
    seen_names, seen_emails, out = set(), set(), []
    for r in records:
        nk, ek = name_key(r["name"]), email_key(r["email"])
        if nk in seen_names or ek in seen_emails:
            continue
        seen_names.add(nk)
        seen_emails.add(ek)
        out.append(r)
    return out

Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. from contacts import dedupe


def test_accent_variants_merge():
    recs = [{"name": "José Núñez", "email": "a@x.com"},
            {"name": "Jose Nunez", "email": "b@x.com"},
            {"name": "JOSÉ  NÚÑEZ", "email": "c@x.com"}]
    assert dedupe(recs) == [recs[0]]


def test_canonical_unicode_variants_merge():
    recs = [{"name": "José Núñez", "email": "a@x.com"},
            {"name": "Jose\u0301 Nu\u0301n\u0303ez", "email": "b@x.com"}]
    assert dedupe(recs) == [recs[0]]


def test_casefold_variants_merge():
    recs = [{"name": "Straße", "email": "a@x.com"},
            {"name": "STRASSE", "email": "b@x.com"}]
    assert dedupe(recs) == [recs[0]]


def test_first_seen_survives_email_match():
    recs = [{"name": "First Person", "email": "Same@x.com"},
            {"name": "Second Person", "email": "same@x.com"}]
    assert dedupe(recs) == [recs[0]]

"""Small backtracking dependency resolver."""

import re


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    """Raised when the requested dependency graph has no valid solution."""


class Version:
    """A dotted-integer version, ordered numerically by component."""

    _PATTERN = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*\Z")

    def __init__(self, s):
        value = str(s)
        if not self._PATTERN.fullmatch(value):
            raise ValueError("invalid version: %s" % value)
        self.original = value
        parts = tuple(int(part) for part in value.split("."))
        while len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] == 0:
            parts = parts[:-1]
        self._parts = parts

    def __str__(self):
        return self.original

    def __repr__(self):
        return "Version(%r)" % self.original

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self._parts)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self._parts == other._parts

    def __lt__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        width = max(len(self._parts), len(other._parts))
        left = self._parts + (0,) * (width - len(self._parts))
        right = other._parts + (0,) * (width - len(other._parts))
        return left < right

    def __le__(self, other):
        return self == other or self < other

    def __gt__(self, other):
        return not self <= other

    def __ge__(self, other):
        return not self < other


class Constraint:
    """A package name and its conjunction of version comparisons."""

    _ITEM = re.compile(r"(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\Z")

    def __init__(self, name, comparisons=()):
        self.name = name
        self.comparisons = tuple(comparisons)

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        if not isinstance(requirement, str):
            raise ValueError("requirement must be a string")
        match = re.fullmatch(r"([A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+)(.*)", requirement.strip())
        if not match:
            raise ValueError("invalid requirement: %s" % requirement)
        name, tail = match.groups()
        comparisons = []
        if tail:
            if not tail.startswith(("==", "!=", "<", ">")):
                raise ValueError("invalid requirement: %s" % requirement)
            for item in tail.split(","):
                parsed = cls._ITEM.fullmatch(item)
                if not parsed:
                    raise ValueError("invalid requirement: %s" % requirement)
                comparisons.append((parsed.group(1), Version(parsed.group(2))))
        return cls(name, comparisons)

    def allows(self, version):
        version = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version(version)
        for op, bound in self.comparisons:
            if op == "==" and version != bound:
                return False
            if op == "!=" and version == bound:
                return False
            if op == "<" and not version < bound:
                return False
            if op == "<=" and not version <= bound:
                return False
            if op == ">" and not version > bound:
                return False
            if op == ">=" and not version >= bound:
                return False
        return True


def resolve(roots, index):
    """Resolve roots to one version per reachable package.

    Variables are selected in alphabetical package order. Candidates are tried
    from highest to lowest, which directly implements the specified
    lexicographic preference while allowing later constraints to backtrack.
    """
    parsed_index = {}
    for name, versions in index.items():
        parsed = []
        for version_text, requirements in versions.items():
            parsed.append((Version(version_text), tuple(
                Constraint.parse(requirement) for requirement in requirements
            )))
        parsed.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
        parsed_index[name] = parsed

    root_constraints = [Constraint.parse(root) for root in roots]
    failure = [None]

    def search(assignments, constraints):
        # Reject conflicts as soon as a constrained package has no viable value.
        for name in sorted(constraints):
            allowed = [version for version, _ in parsed_index.get(name, ())
                       if all(req.allows(version) for req in constraints[name])]
            if not allowed:
                failure[0] = name
                return None
            if name in assignments and assignments[name] not in allowed:
                failure[0] = name
                return None

        unresolved = [name for name in constraints if name not in assignments]
        if not unresolved:
            return assignments
        name = min(unresolved)
        candidates = [item for item in parsed_index.get(name, ())
                      if all(req.allows(item[0]) for req in constraints[name])]
        if not candidates:
            failure[0] = name
            return None

        for version, dependencies in candidates:
            next_assignments = dict(assignments)
            next_assignments[name] = version
            next_constraints = {key: list(value) for key, value in constraints.items()}
            for dependency in dependencies:
                next_constraints.setdefault(dependency.name, []).append(dependency)
            result = search(next_assignments, next_constraints)
            if result is not None:
                return result
        return None

    constraints = {}
    for root in root_constraints:
        constraints.setdefault(root.name, []).append(root)
    result = search({}, constraints)
    if result is None:
        raise ResolutionError("cannot satisfy constraints for package %s" % (failure[0] or "<unknown>"))
    return {name: str(version) for name, version in result.items()}

import unittest

from resolver.solve import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve


class VersionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_numeric_order_and_equivalent_trailing_zeroes(self):
        self.assertLess(Version("1.9"), Version("1.10"))
        self.assertEqual(Version("1.0"), Version("1"))
        self.assertEqual(str(Version("1.0")), "1.0")
        self.assertEqual(len({Version("1"), Version("1.0")}), 1)

    def test_constraint_parsing(self):
        constraint = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3")
        self.assertEqual(constraint.name, "json")
        self.assertTrue(constraint.allows(Version("2.4")))
        self.assertFalse(constraint.allows(Version("3")))


class ResolveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_highest_versions_and_transitive_closure(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1": ["web>=2", "db"]},
            "web": {"1": [], "2": ["json<3"], "2.1": ["json>=3"]},
            "json": {"2": [], "3": []},
            "db": {"1": ["json<3"]},
            "unused": {"99": []},
        }
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["app"], index),
                         {"app": "1", "web": "2", "json": "2", "db": "1"})

    def test_backtracking_honors_alphabetical_lexicographic_preference(self):
        index = {
            "root": {"1": ["z", "a"]},
            "a": {"1": [], "2": ["z==1"]},
            "z": {"1": [], "2": []},
        }
        # a is alphabetically first and can take version 2 only if z is 1.
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["root"], index), {"root": "1", "a": "2", "z": "1"})

    def test_cycles_are_tolerated(self):
        index = {"a": {"1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": ["a"]}}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})

    def test_unsatisfied_error_names_leaf(self):
        index = {"a": {"1": ["b<1"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": []}}
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, r"\bb\b"):
            resolve(["a"], index)

    def test_conflicting_root_constraints_fail(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, r"\bx\b"):
            resolve(["x>=2", "x<2"], {"x": {"1": [], "2": []}})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).

Refactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.
"""


def dedupe_rows(rows):
    seen_ids = set()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r.event_id in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(r.event_id)
        out.append(r)
    return out

from reporting import parse_rows, build_report


def test_small_report():
    rows = parse_rows(["e1,acme,api,1.5,100", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e3,beta,web,2,10"])
    rep = build_report(rows)
    assert rep[0] == {"tenant": "acme", "service": "api", "cpu_seconds": 2.0, "bytes_out": 150, "events": 2}
    assert rep[-1]["events"] == 3


def test_report_dedupes_large_input_in_first_seen_order():
    rows = parse_rows(
        f"event-{i},tenant,service,1,10" for i in range(30_000)
    )
    rows.extend(rows[:100])

    rep = build_report(rows)

    assert rep == [
        {"tenant": "tenant", "service": "service", "cpu_seconds": 30000.0, "bytes_out": 300000, "events": 30000},
        {"tenant": "*", "service": "*", "cpu_seconds": 30000.0, "bytes_out": 300000, "events": 30000},
    ]

"""A small, atomic implementation of the JSON Patch operations."""

import copy
import re


class PatchError(Exception):
    pass


class PointerError(PatchError):
    pass


def resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):
    """Resolve an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer against *doc*."""
    tokens = _pointer_tokens(pointer)
    value = doc
    for token in tokens:
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            if token not in value:
                raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
            value = value[token]
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            index = _array_index(token)
            if index is None or index >= len(value):
                raise PointerError("invalid or out-of-range array index")
            value = value[index]
        else:
            raise PointerError("cannot traverse a scalar value")
    return value


def apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):
    """Apply a sequence of JSON Patch operations atomically."""
    if type(in_place) is not bool:
        raise PatchError("in_place must be a boolean")
    if not isinstance(patch, list):
        raise PatchError("patch must be a list")

    result = copy.deepcopy(doc)
    for operation in patch:
        result = _apply_operation(result, operation)

    if in_place:
        if isinstance(doc, dict) and isinstance(result, dict):
            doc.clear()
            doc.update(result)
            return doc
        if isinstance(doc, list) and isinstance(result, list):
            doc[:] = result
            return doc
        raise PatchError("in-place patch requires a dict or list document")
    return result


_INDEX = re.compile(r"(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)\Z")


def _pointer_tokens(pointer):
    if not isinstance(pointer, str):
        raise PointerError("pointer must be a string")
    if pointer == "":
        return []
    if not pointer.startswith("/"):
        raise PointerError("pointer must be empty or start with slash")
    result = []
    for raw in pointer[1:].split("/"):
        # A tilde must begin one of the two defined escape sequences.
        if re.search(r"~(?![01])", raw):
            raise PointerError("invalid tilde escape")
        result.append(raw.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~"))
    return result


def _array_index(token):
    if not _INDEX.fullmatch(token):
        return None
    try:
        return int(token)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _parent_and_token(doc, pointer):
    tokens = _pointer_tokens(pointer)
    if not tokens:
        return None, None
    parent = doc
    for token in tokens[:-1]:
        if isinstance(parent, dict):
            if token not in parent:
                raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
            parent = parent[token]
        elif isinstance(parent, list):
            index = _array_index(token)
            if index is None or index >= len(parent):
                raise PointerError("invalid or out-of-range array index")
            parent = parent[index]
        else:
            raise PointerError("cannot traverse a scalar value")
    return parent, tokens[-1]


def _get(doc, pointer):
    return resolve_pointer(doc, pointer)


def _add(doc, pointer, value):
    parent, token = _parent_and_token(doc, pointer)
    if parent is None:
        return copy.deepcopy(value)
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        parent[token] = copy.deepcopy(value)
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        if token == "-":
            parent.append(copy.deepcopy(value))
        else:
            index = _array_index(token)
            if index is None or index > len(parent):
                raise PointerError("invalid or out-of-range array index")
            parent.insert(index, copy.deepcopy(value))
    else:
        raise PointerError("parent of target is not a container")
    return doc


def _remove(doc, pointer):
    parent, token = _parent_and_token(doc, pointer)
    if parent is None:
        return None, doc
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if token not in parent:
            raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
        return parent.pop(token), doc
    if isinstance(parent, list):
        index = _array_index(token)
        if index is None or index >= len(parent):
            raise PointerError("invalid or out-of-range array index")
        return parent.pop(index), doc
    raise PointerError("parent of target is not a container")


def _equal(left, right):
    # Python considers bools equal to integers; JSON does not.
    if isinstance(left, bool) != isinstance(right, bool):
        return False
    if isinstance(left, (int, float)) and not isinstance(left, bool):
        return isinstance(right, (int, float)) and not isinstance(right, bool) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, dict) and isinstance(right, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(_equal(left[key], right[key]) for key in left)
    if isinstance(left, list) and isinstance(right, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
    return type(left) is type(right) and left == right


def _apply_operation(doc, operation):
    if not isinstance(operation, dict):
        raise PatchError("each operation must be an object")
    op = operation.get("op")
    if not isinstance(op, str):
        raise PatchError("operation must have a string op")
    if op not in {"add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", "test"}:
        raise PatchError("unknown operation")
    if "path" not in operation or not isinstance(operation["path"], str):
        raise PatchError("operation must have a string path")
    path = operation["path"]
    try:
        _pointer_tokens(path)
        if op in {"add", "replace", "test"} and "value" not in operation:
            raise PatchError("operation is missing value")
        if op in {"move", "copy"}:
            source = operation.get("from")
            if not isinstance(source, str):
                raise PatchError("operation must have a string from")
            source_tokens = _pointer_tokens(source)
            destination_tokens = _pointer_tokens(path)
            if op == "move":
                if len(source_tokens) < len(destination_tokens) and destination_tokens[:len(source_tokens)] == source_tokens:
                    raise PatchError("cannot move a value into its own child")
                value, doc = _remove(doc, source)
            else:
                value = copy.deepcopy(_get(doc, source))
            return _add(doc, path, value)
        if op == "add":
            return _add(doc, path, operation["value"])
        if op == "remove":
            _, doc = _remove(doc, path)
            return doc
        if op == "replace":
            _get(doc, path)
            _, doc = _remove(doc, path)
            return _add(doc, path, operation["value"])
        if op == "test":
            if not _equal(_get(doc, path), operation["value"]):
                raise PatchError("test operation failed")
            return doc
    except PointerError as exc:
        raise PatchError(str(exc)) from exc

import copy

import pytest

from jsonpatch import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer


def test_pointer_resolution_and_escaping():
    doc = {"a/b": {"~key": ["zero", "one"]}}
    assert resolve_pointer(doc, "/a~1b/~0key/1") == "one"
    assert resolve_pointer(doc, "") is doc


@pytest.mark.parametrize("pointer", ["a", "/x", "/a~2b", "/a~"])
def test_invalid_pointers_raise(pointer):
    with pytest.raises(PointerError):
        resolve_pointer({"a": [1]}, pointer)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("token", ["01", "-", "1x", "-1"])
def test_invalid_array_pointer_tokens(token):
    with pytest.raises(PointerError):
        resolve_pointer(["zero", "one"], "/" + token)


def test_add_remove_replace_and_root():
    original = {"items": [1, 3]}
    result = apply_patch(original, [
        {"op": "add", "path": "/items/1", "value": 2},
        {"op": "replace", "path": "/items/0", "value": 0},
        {"op": "remove", "path": "/items/2"},
        {"op": "add", "path": "", "value": {"done": True}},
    ])
    assert result == {"done": True}
    assert original == {"items": [1, 3]}


def test_append_move_and_copy_are_correct_and_independent():
    original = {"items": [{"x": 1}, 2]}
    result = apply_patch(original, [
        {"op": "move", "from": "/items/0", "path": "/items/1"},
        {"op": "copy", "from": "/items/1", "path": "/items/-"},
    ])
    assert result == {"items": [2, {"x": 1}, {"x": 1}]}
    result["items"][1]["x"] = 99
    assert result["items"][2]["x"] == 1
    assert original == {"items": [{"x": 1}, 2]}


def test_move_cannot_target_descendant():
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({"a": {}}, [{"op": "move", "from": "/a", "path": "/a/b"}])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("target", "expected", "passes"), [
    (1, 1.0, True),
    (True, 1, False),
    ({"n": [1]}, {"n": [1.0]}, True),
])
def test_test_operation_json_equality(target, expected, passes):
    patch = [{"op": "test", "path": "/v", "value": expected}]
    if passes:
        apply_patch({"v": target}, patch)
    else:
        with pytest.raises(PatchError):
            apply_patch({"v": target}, patch)


def test_failure_is_atomic_for_copy_and_in_place():
    for in_place in (False, True):
        original = {"values": [1]}
        before = copy.deepcopy(original)
        with pytest.raises(PatchError):
            apply_patch(original, [
                {"op": "add", "path": "/values/-", "value": 2},
                {"op": "remove", "path": "/missing"},
            ], in_place=in_place)
        assert original == before


def test_in_place_success_preserves_document_identity():
    original = {"a": [1]}
    assert apply_patch(original, [{"op": "add", "path": "/a/-", "value": 2}], in_place=True) is original
    assert original == {"a": [1, 2]}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("patch", [
    {"op": "add", "path": "/a", "value": 1},
    [{"op": "unknown", "path": "/a"}],
    [{"op": "add", "path": "/a"}],
    [{"op": "copy", "path": "/a"}],
])
def test_invalid_patch_shapes_raise(patch):
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({}, patch)
